relationshipTypes.label: prerequisite for
relationshipTypes.description: Understanding the source concept helps with the target concept.

relationshipTypes.label: supports
relationshipTypes.description: The source concept provides a result or tool used by the target concept.

relationshipTypes.label: special case of
relationshipTypes.description: The source concept is a more specific form of the target concept.

relationshipTypes.label: counterpart of
relationshipTypes.description: The concepts play related roles in different inferential approaches.

relationshipTypes.label: method for
relationshipTypes.description: The source concept is a method used to carry out the target task.

nodes.label: Probability theory
nodes.description: The mathematical language used to describe uncertainty.

nodes.label: Events and set operations
nodes.description: Events, complements, intersections and unions within a sample space.

nodes.label: Conditional probability
nodes.description: Probability updated after learning that another event occurred.

nodes.label: Independence
nodes.description: A relationship in which learning about one event does not change the probability of another.

nodes.label: Law of total probability
nodes.description: Decomposes a probability across an exhaustive partition.

nodes.label: Bayes’ theorem
nodes.description: Reverses a conditional probability using a prior probability and the law of total probability.

nodes.label: Random variables
nodes.description: Numerical quantities whose values are governed by probability.

nodes.label: Probability distributions
nodes.description: Course PMFs and PDFs, parameter conventions, model choices and an interactive distribution explorer.

nodes.label: Expectation
nodes.description: The probability-weighted population mean of a random variable.

nodes.label: Variance
nodes.description: The expected squared deviation of a random variable from its mean.

nodes.label: Covariance and correlation
nodes.description: Measures of how two random variables vary together.

nodes.label: Statistical inference
nodes.description: Learning about an unknown population or mechanism using observed data.

nodes.label: Population, sample and data
nodes.description: The distinction between the target population, sampled units and recorded observations.

nodes.label: Statistical models
nodes.description: Probability distributions indexed by parameters and used to represent data-generating processes.

nodes.label: Philosophies of inference
nodes.description: The different interpretations and procedures used to learn from data.

nodes.label: Frequentist inference
nodes.description: Treats parameters as fixed and evaluates procedures through repeated sampling.

nodes.label: Bayesian inference
nodes.description: Represents uncertainty about parameters using probability distributions.

nodes.label: Inference tasks
nodes.description: Point estimation, interval estimation and hypothesis testing.

nodes.label: Estimators and estimates
nodes.description: Statistics used to estimate unknown population parameters.

nodes.label: Sampling distributions
nodes.description: The probability distribution of a statistic under repeated sampling.

nodes.label: Bias
nodes.description: The systematic difference between an estimator’s expectation and its target.

nodes.label: Standard error
nodes.description: The standard deviation of an estimator’s sampling distribution.

nodes.label: Mean squared error
nodes.description: A loss criterion combining an estimator’s variance and squared bias.

nodes.label: Central limit theorem
nodes.description: Explains why suitably scaled sample means are approximately Normal in large samples.

nodes.label: Consistency
nodes.description: An estimator approaches the true parameter as the sample size grows.

nodes.label: Likelihood
nodes.description: The statistical model viewed as a function of its unknown parameter for fixed observed data.

nodes.label: Sufficiency
nodes.description: Data reduction that retains all model information about a parameter.

nodes.label: Maximum likelihood estimation
nodes.description: Chooses the parameter value that maximises the likelihood.

nodes.label: Log-likelihood
nodes.description: A logarithmic transformation of likelihood that simplifies products and optimisation.

nodes.label: Score statistic
nodes.description: The derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to the parameter.

nodes.label: Fisher information
nodes.description: Quantifies how much information the model carries about a parameter.

nodes.label: Cramér–Rao lower bound
nodes.description: A lower bound on the variance of unbiased estimators under regularity conditions.

nodes.label: Asymptotic distribution of the MLE
nodes.description: The large-sample Normal approximation for maximum likelihood estimators.

nodes.label: Bayesian updating
nodes.description: Combines a prior distribution and likelihood to obtain a posterior distribution.

nodes.label: Prior distribution
nodes.description: Represents parameter uncertainty before observing the current data.

nodes.label: Posterior distribution
nodes.description: Represents updated parameter uncertainty after combining prior information and data.

nodes.label: Conjugacy
nodes.description: A prior-likelihood pairing that gives a posterior in the same distribution family.

nodes.label: MAP estimator
nodes.description: The parameter value at the mode of the posterior distribution.

nodes.label: Bernstein–von Mises theorem
nodes.description: Connects large-sample Bayesian posteriors with maximum likelihood theory.

nodes.label: Confidence intervals
nodes.description: A repeated-sampling procedure designed to cover the true parameter at a stated rate.

nodes.label: Exact confidence intervals
nodes.description: Confidence intervals whose stated coverage follows exactly from a pivot or sampling distribution.

nodes.label: Approximate confidence intervals
nodes.description: Confidence intervals justified by a large-sample approximation.

nodes.label: Credible intervals
nodes.description: An interval containing a stated amount of posterior probability.

nodes.label: Highest density intervals
nodes.description: A credible interval containing the posterior values with greatest density.

nodes.label: Frequentist hypothesis testing
nodes.description: A decision procedure that evaluates data against a null hypothesis.

nodes.label: Null and alternative hypotheses
nodes.description: Competing parameter statements that define a testing problem.

nodes.label: Test outcomes and errors
nodes.description: Rejection, non-rejection, Type I errors and Type II errors.

nodes.label: p-values
nodes.description: The smallest significance level at which the observed test statistic would lead to rejection.

nodes.label: Power
nodes.description: The probability that a test rejects the null at each possible parameter value.

nodes.label: One-sample z-test
nodes.description: An exact Normal-mean test when the population variance is known.

nodes.label: One-sample t-test
nodes.description: A Normal-mean test using Student’s t distribution when variance is unknown.

nodes.label: Likelihood ratio tests
nodes.description: Tests hypotheses by comparing constrained and unconstrained maximum likelihoods.

nodes.label: Wald tests
nodes.description: Uses an estimator’s approximate Normal distribution and standard error to test a parameter.

nodes.label: Bayes factors
nodes.description: Compares how well two hypotheses predict the observed data.
